description: The pie chart presents the distribution of error types in the MMAR benchmark, showing 7 slices in total with percentage labels on or near the segments. The largest slice is labeled “Perceptual Error” and is colored light purple at approximately 37%. Next is “Reasoning Error” in a slightly darker purple at about 20%, followed by “Correct Answer but Wrong Choice” in bluish-purple at about 15%, and “Repeat Thinking and No Answer” in light blue at about 12%. A smaller light-blue slice labeled “Lack of Knowledge” is about 9%. Two very small slices at the top are labeled with arrow callouts: “Choice Format Error” at about 4% (cyan/light teal) and another tiny light-teal slice (label not clearly readable in the image) at roughly 3% by visual estimation. There is no separate legend, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; the segments appear arranged roughly from larger to smaller around the chart.
